text:
maria: quick q — noticed an eviction spike this morning when two models were sharing the same prefix cache. KV lease handoff looked racy and we got duplicate repopulates. anyone else see this?
kevin: saw that on canary yesterday. root cause was the non-atomic steal path: new owner writes ownership, then old owner releases without checking a sequence/version. race window = a few ms but enough to trigger double-populate under bursts.
samantha: +1 CAS on the owner field would close the window. TTL helps reduce pain but isn't great for long-running sessions that keep the prefix hot.
maria: current pseudo-code is basically:
```
if lease.owner != me:
  acquire_new_lease()
  release_old()
```
which explains the interleaving where both think they own it for a moment.
oz: proposal: include a lease token + version and do a single CAS that swaps owner+token. e.g., `compare_and_swap(prefix, {owner: A, ver: n}, {owner: B, ver: n+1, token: t})`. Old owner must honor token to release cached refs.
kevin: sequencer approach also works: central sequencer hands off and emits an event. solves atomicity but adds a hop and single point. maybe hybrid: optimistic CAS, fallback to sequencer when retries exceed threshold.
samantha: also we should track metrics: `kv.handoff_conflicts`, `kv.duplicate_populates`, `kv.handoff_latency_ms` and add a replay test that spawns N parallel handoffs to assert no duplicates > 0.01%.
maria: sounds good. A few tradeoffs to capture in the RFC: CAS is low-latency but requires us to store a stable expected value; sequencer is robust but adds latency and added infra. TTL/regenerative heuristics reduce tail cost but harm cache hit for long sessions.
kevin: suggest perf target: CAS path p95 < 2ms, fallback to sequencer p95 < 15ms. Also add a circuit-breaker so if prefix is flapping we route to read-through mode.
maria: will draft RFC with: (1) CAS-based atomic handoff design + proto fields, (2) optional sequencer for high-contention prefixes, (3) TTL/decay heuristics for long sessions, (4) metrics and stress tests, (5) rollout plan and canary checks.
samantha: the e2e harness should include racey network delays and CPU pauses (simulate GC).
oz: also consider using per-prefix monotonic lease counters so we can garbage-collect stale leases safely — avoids ABA problem.
maria: good call. I'll include monotonic counter in the fields. I'll ping y'all for review, aiming to post RFC by EOD tomorrow. :raised_hands:
deploy-bot: staged canary deploy for kv-service v2.1.3 completed — 0 errors, 100% healthy.
kevin: thanks — once RFC lands I can prototype the CAS changes in the in-memory shim and run the stress harness.
